items.headline: New York's nuclear Master Plan includes a microreactor study that stops short of backing deployment
items.what_happened: Governor Hochul released New York's Master Plan for Responsible Advanced Nuclear Development at a state nuclear summit in Rochester on November 18, 2026. One of its supporting studies, NYSERDA's Nuclear Microreactor Technologies Study (Report 26-21h), calls the microreactor market pre-commercial and says further work is needed to decide which microreactor technologies and applications, if any, are worth further state action. It recommends a cooperation framework with Fort Drum and Westinghouse Government Services on the Army's Janus project there.
items.why_it_matters: New York names industrial, institutional, military, remote and existing nuclear-site loads as the likeliest microreactor buyers, but commits no money or procurement. For now the state's role is learning from the Fort Drum project.
items.binding_note: A screening-level study; it says it does not establish feasibility or commit the state to policy action or deployment.

sources.label: NYSERDA, Nuclear Microreactor Technologies Study, Report 26-21h (November 2026)
sources.quote: Further work is needed to determine which microreactor technologies and applications, if any, offer sufficient value to New York State to warrant further action.

sources.label: WAMC, At a summit in Rochester, Hochul announces the release of a nuclear power plan for New York (2026-11-18)
sources.quote: The Advanced Nuclear Master Plan addresses issues like commercial viability, workforce readiness and supply chain capacity.

items.headline: Last Energy files NRC request for early foundation work at Texas PWR-20 site
items.what_happened: On October 20, 2026, Last Energy filed part one of a two-part phased construction permit application with the NRC. The limited work authorization request covers permanent foundation work for the PWR-20 reactor vessel at Caldwell County, Texas, including steel H-piles and a steel liner. The NRC published notice of the filing on November 5, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: For a 1-20 MW buyer, this is a formal NRC filing for the PWR-20 at a named Texas site. The NRC has not yet accepted the request for docketing, so no construction start date is set.
items.binding_note: A filed NRC application. The notice says the NRC has not yet decided whether to docket the request, and a detailed technical review follows only after that decision.
